articles.title: Tesla Roadster flies, flips and hits 60 mph in a flash
articles.summary: The new Tesla Roadster drove upside down and launched into the air at SpaceX's Texas facility, but a 2028 production target remains unconfirmed.
articles.body: I've watched plenty of car unveilings over the years, but Tesla's latest Roadster demonstration had me doing a double take. A sleek white sports car climbed a towering curved ramp until it was completely upside down. Then it launched into the air, flipped over and landed safely back on the pavement. And that was only part of the show. Tesla also demonstrated acceleration from zero to 60 mph in a claimed 0.81 seconds. After nearly nine years of waiting, Elon Musk finally showed the world what his redesigned Roadster can do. Now comes the bigger question. Will Tesla actually deliver it? Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will share five practical ways to protect your trip and your wallet this holiday travel season. You’ll learn how to secure your phone and personal information, find better travel deals, avoid common scams, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed. Join us Saturday, October 31, at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Register free now at CyberGuyLive.com. FLYING SPORTS CAR HIDES ITS WINGS AS PRODUCTION GETS CLOSER Tesla Roadster takes flight in dramatic Texas unveiling On Oct. 15, 2026, Tesla unveiled its redesigned Roadster at SpaceX's rocket testing facility in McGregor, Texas. The event brought together engineers from both companies to demonstrate technology more commonly associated with spacecraft. During the demonstration, a Roadster prototype accelerated up a massive curved ramp. A powerful suction system helped keep the vehicle attached as it climbed upside down. Once it reached the top, compressed-gas thrusters propelled it into the air. The vehicle then rotated in midair and landed back on its wheels. Tesla followed that stunt with another impressive maneuver. The Roadster lifted off the ground and flew over a lineup of Tesla vehicles, including a Cybercab, Cybertruck, Tesla Semi, Model Y and Model 3. Nobody was inside the Roadster during these high-risk demonstrations. Musk said Tesla used automated controls to avoid putting anyone in danger. Tesla shared footage of the event on its official X account. You can also watch the full Tesla Roadster unveiling on YouTube. How the Tesla Roadster uses SpaceX technology to fly Here's where the engineering gets especially interesting. Tesla worked with SpaceX to develop a system that uses highly compressed gas to generate thrust. Unlike conventional rocket engines, these cold-gas thrusters don't burn fuel. Instead, they release pressurized gas through nozzles to push the vehicle in a particular direction. The Roadster also uses four powerful electric fans positioned near the rear of the car. They pull air from underneath the vehicle to create suction. That increases the force pressing the tires against the surface, helping the car maintain grip even while upside down. Tesla also uses a ground-sealing system to help maintain suction underneath the vehicle. Meanwhile, the thrusters handle a very different job. Four rear-mounted nozzles provide extra forward acceleration. The most advanced Rocket configuration adds six more thrusters positioned around the vehicle to help control movement in the air. According to Tesla engineering executive Lars Moravy, the standard thruster setup uses a 200-liter high-pressure storage vessel behind the seats. The Rocket configuration adds another 400 liters of storage capacity, bringing the total to approximately 600 liters. That additional equipment takes up the passenger seat area. There's also a practical limitation that gets lost in the excitement. According to Tesla engineering executive Lars Moravy, refilling the Rocket prototype's entire 600-liter high-pressure gas storage system currently takes approximately six to seven hours. Tesla hopes to cut that time significantly. So while the demonstration was extraordinary, the Roadster's brief airborne maneuvers are a long way from sustained flight like an airplane. Inside, Tesla has taken a different approach to the driving experience. The Roadster features a steer-by-wire yoke that electronically transmits steering inputs. Tesla also uses lightweight materials, including magnesium and carbon fiber, along with a fixed seat base to reduce weight. Meanwhile, Track Mode lowers the suspension so drivers can adjust the car for more aggressive handling. How fast is the new Tesla Roadster? Tesla has made some extraordinary performance claims about the Roadster, and its latest unveiling added another. During the event, Tesla showed a thruster-assisted acceleration run that it said took the prototype from zero to 60 mph in approximately 0.81 seconds. That's remarkably quick, even compared with some of the fastest electric supercars. However, the result came from Tesla's own demonstration. Independent testing has yet to verify that acceleration figure on a production vehicle. Tesla also claims the Roadster's more powerful configurations can exceed 230 mph. Musk went even further during the unveiling, suggesting engineers eventually want to reach half the speed of sound. That would be roughly 380 mph, depending on atmospheric conditions. For now, that more ambitious target remains an aspiration rather than a demonstrated capability. Tesla also projects more than 300 miles of driving range on a charge. That's a substantial reduction from the approximately 620 miles promised when the second-generation Roadster was first introduced in 2017. At the time, Tesla also envisioned a four-seat sports car. FLYING TAXIS ARE TAKING OFF IN TEXAS. IS YOUR CITY NEXT? Tesla plans three versions of the new Roadster Here's something worth knowing before getting too excited about the flying demonstration. Tesla offers a road-focused Performance configuration, along with two more extreme options called Thrust and Rocket. Each adds capabilities that take the Roadster further beyond a conventional electric sports car. Roadster Performance The Performance version is designed for conventional road driving. It seats two people and features active aerodynamics along with the advanced suction system. Tesla claims it can accelerate from zero to 60 mph in under 1.6 seconds without the rocket-style thrusters. Roadster Thrust The Thrust configuration takes acceleration considerably further. It adds four rear-mounted cold-gas thrusters to the two-seat design. Tesla claims this version can reach 60 mph in under 0.9 seconds. The company describes it as race-ready and plans a limited release. Roadster Rocket The Rocket version is the one that really pushes the technology. It uses 10 thrusters to provide forward acceleration, upward movement and airborne maneuvering. Tesla claims this configuration could reach 60 mph in under 0.59 seconds. However, all that additional equipment requires a compromise. The Rocket version seats only one person and will be available by invitation. Tesla also explicitly warns that it has not received approval for public road use. Musk acknowledged that safety wasn't necessarily the top priority when developing the Roadster's most extreme capabilities. He also expressed uncertainty about where those features would be legal to use. For now, Tesla has only demonstrated the airborne maneuvers under controlled conditions. Keep in mind that these acceleration figures are Tesla's projected specifications. They have yet to be independently confirmed on production vehicles. How much will the Tesla Roadster cost? This is where potential buyers should pay close attention. When Tesla originally announced the second-generation Roadster in 2017, it discussed a starting price of approximately $200,000. However, Tesla did not announce a new final purchase price at its October 2026 unveiling. Instead, the company reopened reservations with substantial upfront payments. For the Performance version, Tesla requires an initial $5,000 payment followed by another $45,000 within 10 days. That brings the total reservation payment to $50,000. The limited-release Thrust version requires the same initial $5,000 payment. However, buyers must then provide another $245,000 within 10 days. That's a total reservation payment of $250,000, even though the vehicle's final purchase price remains unknown. Tesla has not disclosed pricing for the invitation-only Rocket configuration. According to Tesla's official Roadster Reservation Agreement, a reservation secures an approximate place in line rather than a completed vehicle order. Tesla says customers can cancel their reservations and receive a full refund until they complete their vehicle configuration after Tesla invites them to do so. However, the money won't be held separately in escrow or earn interest. There's another important detail. Tesla explicitly states that the Roadster remains under development and that it cannot guarantee when a vehicle will be delivered, or whether it will be delivered at all. And Tesla has already missed its original deadline by several years. The company initially expected deliveries to begin in 2020. Musk now says production should begin in 2028, although that remains a target rather than a guaranteed date. Why Tesla calls the Roadster one of its last human-driven cars Here's something else that caught my attention. Musk suggested the Roadster could be among Tesla's last cars designed for human drivers. Think about that for a moment. Tesla is spending billions developing cars that drive themselves, yet its most exciting new vehicle is designed for people who actually love being behind the wheel. I find that pretty ironic, especially coming from the man who wants to make autonomous driving the norm. Just look at Tesla's Cybercab. It doesn't even have a steering wheel or traditional driving controls. We've already seen how Tesla's Cybercab is carrying riders in Austin, although questions about safety and operating restrictions remain. Meanwhile, the Roadster is all about the thrill of driving. There's something to be said for feeling the car respond when you hit the accelerator or take a sharp turn. Of course, Musk hasn't confirmed that Tesla will eliminate manual driving from its other vehicles. But if that's where the company is headed, I wonder how many drivers will be willing to give up the steering wheel. JCB HYDROMAX SHATTERS A WORLD RECORD WITH ‘EXTRAORDINARY’ SPEEDS TOPPING 400 MPH IN HYDROGEN-POWERED CAR What this means to you You probably aren't planning to spend hundreds of thousands of dollars on a Tesla Roadster. Still, this project raises some interesting questions about where automotive technology could be headed. For starters, the Roadster's advanced suction system demonstrates how electric fans can dramatically increase traction. Similar technology already exists in specialized high-performance vehicles. Further development could eventually influence other types of performance cars. However, the cold-gas thrusters introduce challenges that may limit their usefulness outside controlled environments. The hardware occupies valuable space, while the pressurized gas supply requires replenishment after use. There's also the gap between demonstrating a prototype and delivering a finished vehicle. Tesla still needs to prove the Roadster can be manufactured reliably and meet applicable regulations. For anyone considering a reservation, I would take a close look at Tesla's current Roadster information and reservation terms before paying. The company's specifications are still subject to change, and the Roadster shown at the unveiling remains a prototype. Kurt's key takeaways I have to give Tesla credit for getting my attention with this one. Watching a sports car drive upside down and then launch itself into the air was pretty incredible. And knowing that engineers from Tesla and SpaceX worked together to pull it off makes the technology even more interesting. But here's what I'm watching. Tesla first showed us the next-generation Roadster back in 2017, and customers are still waiting. Now we're hearing 2028. I'd love to see this car actually make it into production because there's something refreshing about an electric sports car designed for people who still love to drive. But asking customers to put down as much as $250,000 without a final price or guaranteed delivery date is a lot to swallow. As much as I'd love to take one for a spin, I think I'll leave those midair flips to the engineers until Tesla can prove this technology belongs outside a controlled demonstration. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Senior Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) leader Indresh Kumar on Sunday urged citizens to remain vigilant against what he described as “ideologies that threaten the country’s unity and integrity” as he addressed the recent protests by opposition parties and the youth pressure group Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar."India must remain vigilant against ideologies that threaten its unity and integrity. … Any attempt to weaken India's unity, integrity and constitutional framework cannot be accepted," Kumar said at a conference of RSS affiliate Muslim Rashtriya Manch in Lucknow.Reacting to the opposition's protests, Kumar questioned whether the pursuit of political power could take precedence over the country's stability and national interests.“Spreading distrust in the electoral system and constitutional institutions is futile. … India needs responsible leadership, social harmony and nation-building, not confrontation and chaos,” he added.Citing the situations in Bangladesh and Pakistan, Kumar warned that violence, extremism, political confrontation and social divisions could undermine peace and stability in any country.The opposition and CJP have been demanding CEC Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Protests erupted in several parts of the country, particularly in Delhi, following a report by The Indian Express last month that the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had raised objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions they claimed had been taken without their knowledge.Congress MP and Lok Sabha leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi, who has led opposition protests against the CEC, has repeatedly named RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat among five people he alleges have “hijacked” national institutions. articles.title: St. Petersburg oil facilities ablaze as Ukraine launches more than 1,000 drones at Russia
articles.summary: Ukrainian strikes set an oil export terminal and a depot ablaze in St.
articles.body: Ukrainian strikes set an oil export terminal and a depot ablaze in St. Petersburg on Sunday as Kyiv launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia in one of its largest aerial attacks of the war. The strikes came amid deepening tensions between Ukraine and Washington, with U.S. President Donald Trump criticizing Kyiv’s attacks on Russian oil infrastructure and the prospect of further U.S. sanctions against Moscow still uncertain. One person was killed and five others were wounded in the St. Petersburg attack, which sparked fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal and the city’s Ruchi oil depot, local Gov. Alexander Beglov said. A logistics center belonging to Russian retailer Ozon and a data center operated by Russian tech giant VK were also targeted, the companies confirmed. Russia’s Defense Ministry said Sunday that its forces had destroyed 1,015 Ukrainian drones over 15 Russian regions, the annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the Black Sea. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told Russian state news agency Tass that Kyiv was “resisting” Moscow’s invasion but could not “change the current course of events.” Future of U.S. sanctions still unclear The strikes came after Trump told reporters that they did not know what his decision on further sanctions against Russia would be, despite signing an executive order Friday night waiving planned restrictions, citing U.S. national interests. Speaking on NBC’s “Meet the Press” on Sunday, Zelenskyy said waiving sanctions against Russia would strengthen Putin’s war effort. He also said U.S.-Ukraine intelligence sharing had resumed after being “blocked for some period of time.” Zelenskyy said that while he trusted Trump, siding with Moscow would be a tragedy and a “historic mistake” for Washington. “People want to forget what’s going on. But we can’t give this possibility to forget, or to change reality, or to change the truth,” Zelenskyy said. “We can’t compare me and Putin. He’s aggressor. He occupied us. He killed adults and children, his soldiers. He’s a terrorist. And that’s why I hope that President Trump will be very clear with this position.” A woman was killed and a 6-year-old girl was among at least two other people wounded in two Russian attacks on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, local officials said Sunday. Two apartment buildings, 18 cars and an educational institution were damaged in the attacks, Mykhailo Semikin, head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration, said. Russia continues energy attacks, Kyiv says Trump announced on Oct. 11 that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an “energy ceasefire” in the 4½-year-old war, but offered no details. Kyiv reported Russian attacks on energy sites after his announcement. Ukraine confirmed on Thursday that it had resumed attacks on Russian oil facilities after a three-day pause. Zelenskyy expressed outrage at Russia’s continued aerial bombardment of Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, in apparent defiance of Trump’s call on Sunday for both sides to halt such attacks. The Ukrainian government initially said it was observing the ceasefire. In a post on X on Sunday, Zelenskyy said Russia had attacked Ukraine’s energy, oil and gas sectors 76 times in the week since Trump’s announcement. Energy facilities in four Ukrainian regions had been attacked overnight, leaving tens of thousands of families without power, he said, accusing Russia of trying to cause a blackout. “America should see that Russia is not taking any reciprocal steps in response to sanctions relief or agreements. On the contrary, they take every signal of an opportunity to make money as proof that their bet on war is paying off and they can keep fighting,” he wrote. Zelenskyy also stressed that the war was continuing because of Russia’s invasion, not Ukraine’s efforts to defend itself. “It is Russia that must face pressure for peace to have a chance. Thank you to everyone who understands this and helps,” he said.

articles.title: Madhepura village wages war on liquor, drugs with Rs25k fine
articles.summary: Madhepura’s Sahugarh Panchayat vows to go “Nasha Mukt,” imposing a Rs 25,000 social fine for liquor/drug use or sales and denying bail support.
articles.body: Patna: Fed up with the drug menace, a village in Madhepura district has come up with its own strict justice system. In a bold and unusual decision, residents of Sahugarh Panchayat in Madhepura Sadar block have decided to impose a social fine of Rs 25,000 on anyone caught consuming liquor or drugs or selling narcotics in the village. The villagers have also pledged that if someone is jailed in a drug case, his own family will not come forward to get him bail. The idea is simple - create strong social pressure to keep people away from drugs and choke the supply chain at the village level.The decision was taken on Oct 17 at a meeting held on the school premises of Sahugarh Panchayat. The meeting was chaired by mukhiya Mukesh Kumar and attended by present and former mukhiyas, Panchayat representatives, BJP Madhepura District President Deepak Kumar and a large number of villagers. In the meeting, everyone took a collective pledge to make Sahugarh ‘Nasha Mukt’.It was decided that collective efforts would be made to stop all kinds of intoxication and their sale. Violators will face social action and the administration will also be informed for legal action.The villagers also prepared a written resolution letter - a ‘Sankalp Patra’ - which was signed by the Panches and hundreds of villagers.Villagers said just talking about drugs would not solve the problem. “Only discussion will not work; the whole village will have to unite,” said Santosh Rai, one of the participants.Sahugarh mukhiya Mukesh Kumar said, “Making the panchayat drug-free is not the responsibility of one person. articles.title: Meloni condemns ‘gangs of thugs’ after protests turned violent across Italy
articles.summary: Giorgia Meloni backed law enforcement after violent anti-government protests erupted across Italy, with clashes in Milan, Bologna and Turin injuring police officers.
articles.body: Italy, like France, witnessed a day of protests on Saturday — several turning violent — as some Italian politicians blamed the extreme left for the lawlessness. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni took to social media to condemn the unrest and back law enforcement. Meloni wrote on X: "Once again, the women and men of the Law Enforcement Forces have had to face the violence of criminals who, even through organized groups, exploit demonstrations to seek confrontation and sow chaos," she posted. She added, "Because they were there to safeguard the safety of citizens, workers, merchants and all the people who have the right to live [in] their city without fear and without seeing it laid to waste and set ablaze by gangs of thugs," she continued. "We stand with you." VIOLENCE ERUPTS AT FRANCE PROTESTS AS MACRON WARNS UNREST IS BEING EXPLOITED Her Sunday morning post came after scenes of violence between protesters and police, the most visible being outside Milan’s historic Cathedral, known as the Piazza del Duomo. The Associated Press reported 50 demonstrators, including minors, were detained and at least two police officers were hurt in a protest that required water cannons to disperse the crowd, quoting the LaPresse news agency. Rioters looted stores and smashed windows inside Milan’s Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, one of Italy’s most famous 19th‑century arcades. Meloni had already laid blame for the protests on Saturday night, posting: "Thugs who exploit demonstrations to sow chaos, attack those who ensure security and hold entire cities hostage… Demonstrating is a right. Setting our cities ablaze is not." She added a message to her political opponents: "I renew my request to the opposition: do not be ambiguous about this. Unequivocally condemn these acts of violence and issue a clear appeal for every mobilization to be peaceful." LIMOGES TOWN HALL 'LARGELY LOST' AFTER FAR-LEFT RIOTERS SET HISTORIC BUILDING ON FIRE AMID FRENCH UNREST Il Sole 24 news site quoted Francesco Filini, MP for Meloni's Fratelli d’Italia and national program coordinator, as saying: "It is no longer tolerable that every time left-wing extremists take to the streets, scenes of organized destruction unfold. We are not dealing with mere demonstrators, but with organized groups that plan violence." Saturday's demonstrations were organized by the Confederazione Generale Italiana del Lavoro, or CGIL, Italy’s oldest labor union with over 5 million members, often connected to Italian political parties on the left. Meloni posted she had "great respect for the thousands" who protested peacefully and calling participation "the foundation of any healthy democracy… we cannot ignore what happened in other Italian squares." She noted that in Milan "stones were thrown at the Law Enforcement Forces, officers were injured, damage and violence occurred that forced the interruption of the procession. In Turin, people were stopped carrying cobblestones and window-breaking hammers. In Bologna, the disorders led to the precautionary closure of the railway station." "In the face of scenes like these, the rejection must be unanimous," Meloni posted. "Any hesitation becomes justification. Silence is not acceptable." ITALY ROCKED BY ANARCHIST-LED RIOTS AS OVER 100 POLICE INJURED, MELONI CONDEMNS VIOLENCE Milan’s center-left mayor, Giuseppe Sala, told the Associated Press, "The reasons for the protests were understandable. The violence against law enforcement and serious damage to the city are not justifiable." articles.title: Saptami fervour grips city as theme pandals draw crowds
articles.summary: Mahasaptami crowds throng Bhubaneswar-Cuttack Durga Puja pandals with theme décor, rituals, cultural shows; police step up security for smooth movement.
articles.body: Bhubaneswar: Durga Puja pandals with innovative themes, dazzling illumination, cultural programmes and food stalls emerged as major crowd-pullers on Mahasaptami, which was marked by special rituals across the state.At Damana Durga Puja Committee in Bhubaneswar, devotees participated in a Kalash Yatra, in which 108 women carried holy water in earthen pots to ceremonially welcome Goddess Durga, said Nishakar Sahoo, president of Damana Durga Puja Committee.This year, theme-based pandals have become the centrepiece of celebrations in Bhubaneswar. Puja committees have recreated iconic landmarks and spiritual destinations, offering visitors a unique blend of art, culture and devotion. From futuristic architectural inspirations based on Dubai’s skyline at Bomikhal to Odia pride shown at Saheed Nagar, the themes reflect both global influences and local cultural inspirations.Several pandals are also showcasing religious heritage and architectural grandeur. One committee has recreated elements of Uttarakhand’s 'Char Dham’ pilgrimage, while another has drawn inspiration from an ancient Shiva temple in Cambodia.In Cuttack, traditional silver filigree tableaux, popularly known as Chandi Medha, continue to be a major attraction. Puja organisers have invested heavily in decoration and lighting in a bid to make this year's festivities more spectacular than ever.More than 350 Durga Pujas are being organised across Bhubaneswar and Cuttack this year. Apart from the rituals, several pandals are hosting bhajan performances, dramas, dance programmes and musical evenings, transforming the puja venues into vibrant cultural hubs.The festive atmosphere extends beyond the twin cities, with grand celebrations taking place in Berhampur, Puri, Balasore, Rourkela and Sambalpur. Devotees are also visiting renowned Shakti shrines, including Tara Tarini, Biraja and Bimala temples, where special rituals are being performed.Anticipating massive crowds, the commissionerate police, meanwhile, have made extensive security arrangements to ensure the smooth movement of devotees and maintain law and order. articles.title: Clouds clip Surya Kiran show for Mysuru Dasara but crew hopes to return today
articles.summary: IAF’s Surya Kiran aerobatic team delayed Mysuru Dasara air show 45 minutes due to rain and clouds, limiting to three manoeuvres; hopes full display Monday.
articles.body: Mysuru/Bengaluru: The Surya Kiran aerobatic team had spent hours preparing its aircraft and pilots for a nine-jet spectacle over Mysuru, but the weather had other plans. Overnight rain and cloudy skies forced the Indian Air Force team to delay Sunday’s Dasara air show by 45 minutes and limit its performance to three basic horizontal manoeuvres, leaving the crowd waiting for the full display.The team, however, remained hopeful of returning Monday with its complete repertoire, weather permitting.“We were very happy to be here for the auspicious occasion of Mysuru Dasara and were looking forward to performing before the crowd. Unfortunately, the weather forced us to limit the display to three manoeuvres. We regret not being able to complete the full performance,” said wing commander Abhimanyu Tyagi of the Surya Kiran team.Clear skies are essential for the team’s intricate aerobatics, particularly its high-altitude vertical formations. Despite the curtailed show, spectators who had gathered from across the state applauded the pilots for taking to the skies despite the conditions.Pooja R, an IT professional from Bengaluru, said, “We had come to see the air show, but due to heavy overnight rain and cloudy skies, the programme was delayed. We thank the entire Surya Kiran team for making the effort to perform a few manoeuvres despite the unfavourable conditions.”While the weather determines what the audience sees, preparations for a display begin hours before take-off. Around 180 ground personnel, working in three teams, carry out detailed inspections and coordinate with pilots to ensure the aircraft are ready.For Naveen Kumar, who has spent six and a half years with the team, the working day begins around 4 am, even when the scheduled take-off is at 9 am.“In the daily inspection, the integrity of the panels, all engine oil, hydraulic oil, all the levels should be within parameters,” he said.The coordination continues through the day. Squadron Leader Bhavesh Sharma, who flies in the number five position in the team’s signature nine-aircraft diamond formation, said pilots first report to the daily servicing section, where the ground crew is based.“This inherent bond between the technician and the air crew is very important, because we need to have full trust in the people who are maintaining our aircraft,” he said.Technicians undergo six months of basic training, 16 months of technical training and a further four to six months of specialised aircraft training before being posted to the team. Pilots, meanwhile, undergo six to eight months of intensive training after joining.Based in Bidar, the team operates from Yelahanka for the Mysuru Dasara event. It comprises 18 officers, including 13 pilots, three engineering officers, a commentator and a medical officer. Group captain Ajay Dasarathi is the team leader and commanding officer.The team, one of only four in the world capable of performing nine-aircraft aerobatic displays, is hoping the weather will allow it to deliver the full spectacle Monday.BoxMysuru Palace, Vampire among planned formationsThe Surya Kiran team has planned special formations for Mysuru, including an outline of Mysuru Palace and a Vampire aircraft formation, alongside other minor changes to its usual display.
